arxiv-2009-00757.title: Properties of f-divergences and f-GAN training
arxiv-2009-00757.creator: Matt Shannon Google Research mattshannon@google.com
arxiv-2009-00757.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Matt Shannon Google Research mattshannon@google.com. In this technical report we describe some properties of f-divergences and f-GAN training. We present an elementary derivation of the f-divergence lower bounds which form the basis of f-GAN training. We derive informative but perhaps underappreciated properties of f-divergences and f-GAN training, including a gradient matching property and the fact that all f-divergences agree up to an overall scale factor on the divergence between nearby distributions.

arxiv-2209-09688.title: Sparse Vicious Attacks on Graph Neural Networks Corresponding Author at giovanni.trappolini@uniroma1.it
arxiv-2209-09688.creator: Giovanni Trappolini
arxiv-2209-09688.description: Abstract Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have proven to be successful in several predictive modeling tasks for graph-structured data. Amongst those tasks, link prediction is one of the fundamental problems for many real-world applications, such as recommender systems. However, GNNs are not immune to adversarial attacks, i.e., carefully crafted malicious examples that are designed to fool the predictive model.

arxiv-2301-02312.title: Training trajectories, mini-batch losses and the curious role of the learning rate.
arxiv-2301-02312.creator: Mark Sandler, Andrey Zhmoginov, Max Vladymyrov, Nolan Miller
arxiv-2301-02312.description: Abstract Stochastic gradient descent plays a fundamental role in nearly all applications of deep learning. However its ability to converge to a global minimum remains shrouded in mystery. In this paper we propose to study the behavior of the loss function on fixed mini-batches along SGD trajectories.

arxiv-2311-07099.title: Explanation-aware Soft Ensemble Empowers Large Language Model In-context Learning
arxiv-2311-07099.creator: Yue Yu, Jiaming Shen, Tianqi Liu, Zhen Qin, Jing Nathan Yan, Jialu Liu, Chao Zhang, Michael Bendersky
arxiv-2311-07099.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) have shown remarkable capabilities in various natural language understanding tasks. With only a few demonstration examples, these LLMs can quickly adapt to target tasks without expensive gradient updates. Common strategies to boost such “in-context” learning ability are to ensemble multiple model decoded results and require the model to generate an explanation along with the prediction.

arxiv-2408-12845.title: Keep Everyone Happy: Online Fair Division of Numerous Items with Few Copies
arxiv-2408-12845.creator: Arun Verma, Indrajit Saha, Makoto Yokoo, Bryan Kian Hsiang Low
arxiv-2408-12845.description: Abstract This paper considers a novel variant of the online fair division problem involving multiple agents in which a learner sequentially observes an indivisible item that must be irrevocably allocated to one of the agents to achieve a desired balance between fairness and efficiency.

arxiv-2410-07772.title: Towards Quantifying The Privacy Of Redacted Text

arxiv-2410-07772.description: Abstract In this paper we propose use of a k-anonymity-like approach for evaluating the privacy of redacted text. arxiv-2509-13987.title: Differential Privacy in Federated Learning: Mitigating Inference Attacks with Randomized Response
arxiv-2509-13987.creator: Ozer Ozturk, Busra Buyuktanir, Gozde Karatas Baydogmus, Kazim Yildiz
arxiv-2509-13987.description: Abstract Machine learning models used for distributed architectures consisting of servers and clients require large amounts of data to achieve high accuracy. Data obtained from clients are collected on a central server for model training. However, storing data on a central server raises concerns about security and privacy. To address this issue, a federated learning architecture has been proposed.

pmc-11636251.creator: Kyuhyoung Jeong, Sunghwan Cho, Dohun Song, Ruonan Li, Sangyoon Han, Heeran J Cho, Jongho Kim
pmc-11636251.description: PurposeThis study analyzed the longitudinal relationship between smartphone addiction and sleep duration to investigate the factors contributing to sleep deprivation in Korean children.MethodsTo overcome the limitations of previous studies, panel quantile regression analysis was used to evaluate the relationship between smartphone addiction and sleep duration. Key variables were smartphone addiction, sleep duration, gender, and age.

pmc-12619220.title: Aldolase a in pan-cancer and lung squamous cell carcinoma: prognostic value and macrophage-driven immune suppression unveiled by multi-omics and cohort validation
pmc-12619220.creator: Ying Ji, Xincheng Li, Xihao Shen, Xiumei Hu, Yujing Du, Bin Hu, Wei Wang, Fanjie Meng
pmc-12619220.description: BackgroundAldolase A (ALDOA), a key glycolytic enzyme, has been implicated in tumor progression and metabolic reprogramming across multiple cancers [1]. However, its role in lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) remains largely unexplored. Recent studies suggest that ALDOA may influence the tumor immune microenvironment, particularly through its association with macrophages [2, 3].

pmc-12786779.title: Degradation Behavior of Surface Wear Resistance of Marine Airport Rigid Pavements
pmc-12786779.creator: Yuming Guo, Jingxuan Zhao, Tiancong Hao, Qingya Sun
pmc-12786779.description: Rigid pavements in marine airports are subjected to severe surface degradation due to the combined effects of salt erosion and repeated aircraft impact loading, which significantly reduces service life and operational safety. This study investigates the degradation behavior and underlying mechanisms governing the surface wear resistance of C40 concrete under simulated marine environmental and mechanical conditions.

pmc-13123489.title: Gilteritinib-associated hand-foot syndrome: a novel dermatologic reaction in refractory FLT3 Acute myeloid leukemia
pmc-13123489.creator: Jack T Seki, Jad Sibai, Maria Agustina Perusini, Hassan Sibai
pmc-13123489.description: Highlights•Unexpected toxicity: Gilteritinib, a second-generation FLT3-specific TKI with minimal EGFR/VEGFR inhibition, was presumed to have low dermatologic toxicity.
